importance_ranking.reason: Completed project photos are the primary trust signal for a design and construction service — buyers use images to identify structure type (polyhouse vs shade net vs glass), assess build quality, and verify scale. High visual variation across sub-types means wrong or absent images cause immediate skip.

Greenhouse Type and Design Compliance (NHB/MIDH) are non-negotiable shortlisting gates — a buyer cannot determine subsidy eligibility or structural fit without these specs. Listings without them cannot be evaluated by the majority buyer segment.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per sq ft; consultancy and small walk-in tunnel projects may quote per project lump sum. Per sq m is dominant for commercial projects and NHB subsidy calculations — must be shown to enable price comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit. Per sq m vs per sq ft vs per project lump sum creates real confusion for buyers comparing multiple service providers.

Per sq m rate varies substantially by greenhouse type and compliance tier (walk-in tunnel vs hi-tech climate-controlled = large cost difference). Indian buyers are price-sensitive but compare rates only after confirming greenhouse type and NHB compliance fit.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — buyers search by compliance tier, greenhouse type, and geographic coverage, not by manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Large capital project with high post-sale dependency (erection, commissioning, subsidy documentation) means seller track record, NHB empanelment, and past project portfolio are evaluated during vendor selection, but only after spec and compliance fit is confirmed.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the service delivers — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements, with the largest price delta in the category (walk-in tunnel vs hi-tech glass greenhouse represents a 10x+ cost difference).

NHB/MIDH compliance is a binary subsidy eligibility gate — mandated structural specifications (hot-dip GI pipe, UV-stabilized film) drive significant cost differences and a buyer applying for government subsidy cannot substitute a non-compliant design.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Cladding type (UV-stabilized PE film vs polycarbonate sheet vs shade net vs glass) is independently configurable from greenhouse type and drives significant cost and performance differences — buyers specify this as a primary structural requirement.

Buyers need to know whether the provider offers full turnkey construction or design/consultancy only — these are fundamentally different service engagements with different pricing structures and buyer requirements.

Structural design parameters (wind load, ventilation configuration, span width) vary by agro-climatic zone across India — a design valid for Maharashtra may not meet wind load requirements in coastal Andhra Pradesh or high-altitude Himachal Pradesh.
